```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
R <- params$results
rd <- function(...) {
  f <- file.path(R, ...)
  if (file.exists(f)) read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE) else NULL
}
# Figures from the run folders (several at once; missing ones are skipped).
fig <- function(...) {
  f <- file.path(R, ...)
  f <- f[file.exists(f)]
  if (length(f)) knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(f), rel_path = FALSE)
}
# HTML tables, so each caption stays with its own table.
tab <- function(x, digits = 3, ...) {
  knitr::kable(x, format = "html", digits = digits, row.names = FALSE,
               table.attr = "class='table table-condensed' style='width:auto'", ...)
}
r0_row <- function(x, model = NULL) {
  x <- x[x$parameter == "R0", ]
  if (!is.null(model)) x <- x[x$model == model, ]
  x
}
fmt <- function(x, d = 3) formatC(x, digits = d, format = "f")
```

This report collects the results of every run in `examples/results/` (each folder has its
own detailed report). It reads the saved tables only, so it can be rebuilt at any time:

```r
rmarkdown::render("All_results.Rmd", output_dir = "results")
```

**How to read the numbers.** *R0 MAE* is the average absolute error of the R0 estimate on
simulated epidemics with known parameters (lower is better). *Coverage* is the share of
observed days inside a model's 95% band of simulated curves; the *interval score* adds the
band width and a penalty for every observed day outside it (lower is better), so a band
cannot score well just by being wide.

# Summary

```{r summary-numbers}
sir_ref <- rd("reproduce_pretrained_sir_75k", "seed_variation.csv")
v2_test <- rd("seir_bilstm_v2", "test_metrics.csv")
rep_models <- c(`SEIR v4` = "seir_bilstm_v4", `SEIR v5` = "seir_bilstm_v5",
                `SEIR v5 (128 hidden units)` = "seir_bilstm_v5_h128")
rep_models <- rep_models[file.exists(file.path(R, rep_models, "test_R0_v2_vs_model.csv"))]
rep_test <- lapply(rep_models, function(d) rd(d, "test_R0_v2_vs_model.csv"))
best_rep <- names(rep_test)[which.min(vapply(rep_test, function(x) x$model_R0_MAE[1], 0))]
meth <- rd("seir_v4_method_comparison", "summary.csv")
acc  <- rd("seir_v4_method_comparison", "accuracy_simulated.csv")
v5   <- rd("seir_bilstm_v5", "summary.csv")
v4   <- rd("seir_bilstm_v4", "summary.csv")
sm   <- rd("sir_method_comparison", "summary.csv")
s2m  <- rd("seir_method_comparison_v2", "summary.csv")
get  <- function(x, measure, col) x[[col]][x$measure == measure]
mrow <- function(m, col) meth[[col]][meth$method == m]
v5_sim  <- mrow("SEIR v5", "sim R0 MAE")
nd0m <- rd("sir_no_day0_method_comparison", "summary.csv")
f5   <- rd("seir_bilstm_v5", "real_data_fits.csv")
f5   <- f5[f5$window != "", ]
v2_real_cov <- mean(f5$coverage_pct[f5$band == "v2"])
v5_real_cov <- mean(f5$coverage_pct[grepl("range", f5$band)])
best_search <- meth$method[meth$method %in% c("ABC-MCMC", "ABC-SMC", "NelderMead", "DE")][
  which.min(meth$`sim R0 MAE`[meth$method %in% c("ABC-MCMC", "ABC-SMC", "NelderMead", "DE")])]
```

All the work in one table:

| Data | Model to use | Key result |
|---|---|---|
| SIR, 61 days | SIR BiLSTM (reproduced pretrained recipe, 60,000 curves) | R0 MAE `r fmt(sir_ref$R0_MAE[2])` vs `r fmt(sir_ref$R0_MAE[1])` for the original pretrained model; on the 100-curve comparison `r fmt(sm$R0_MAE[1])`, better than every search method (best: DE `r fmt(sm$R0_MAE[sm$method == "DE"])`), in `r fmt(sm$seconds_per_curve[1], 2)` s instead of minutes |
| SEIR, every case counted (simulated) | SEIR v2 | R0 MAE `r fmt(s2m$R0_MAE[1])` vs DE `r fmt(s2m$R0_MAE[s2m$method == "DE"])`, Nelder-Mead `r fmt(s2m$R0_MAE[s2m$method == "Nelder-Mead"])`, ABC-SMC `r fmt(s2m$R0_MAE[s2m$method == "ABC-SMC"])` |
| SIR, real data of any length (30-365 days, one wave) | SIR v6 | R0 MAE on reported-case windows from the beginning 0.21 (30 days), 0.12 (61 days), 0.06 (120+ days); on real data and the six states it fits as well as SEIR v6, with a lower R0 (no incubation period) |
| SEIR, real data of any length (30-365 days, one wave) | SEIR v6 | reads any length and position; R0 MAE on reported-case windows falls from about 0.5 (30 days) to 0.06 (270-365 days); fits whole flu seasons and the waves of six US states |
| **SEIR, real reported data** | **SEIR v5** | R0 MAE `r fmt(v5_sim)` on reported-case curves (best search method, `r best_search`: `r fmt(mrow(best_search, "sim R0 MAE"))`); true R0 inside its 95% range `r fmt(get(v5, "True R0 inside the 95% range (%)", "model_with_range"), 0)`% of the time; `r fmt(mrow("SEIR v5", "seconds per curve"), 2)` s per curve |

Main points:

1. **The BiLSTM is the most accurate method on simulated epidemics in almost every setting,
   and thousands of times faster** than ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC, Nelder-Mead and DE. The exception
   is SIR without day 0, where Nelder-Mead and DE are slightly more accurate (R0 MAE
   `r fmt(nd0m$R0_MAE[nd0m$method == "Nelder-Mead"])` and `r fmt(nd0m$R0_MAE[nd0m$method == "DE"])` vs
   `r fmt(nd0m$R0_MAE[1])`) but take `r fmt(nd0m$seconds_per_curve[nd0m$method == "Nelder-Mead"], 0)` and
   `r fmt(nd0m$seconds_per_curve[nd0m$method == "DE"], 0)` seconds per curve.
2. **Real data are reported cases, not every infection.** The models trained on every case
   (v2) break on reported-case curves (R0 MAE `r fmt(rep_test[[1]]$v2_R0_MAE[1], 2)`). Training on
   reported cases with wider ranges (v4) and drawing new reporting noise every epoch (v5)
   fixed this: on the 7 real windows (Utah COVID-19, Utah flu, Baltimore 1918) v5's 95% bands
   hold `r fmt(v5_real_cov, 0)`% of the observed days on average, v2's `r fmt(v2_real_cov, 0)`%.
3. **Recovering the curves:** on real data v5 and ABC-SMC are close (interval score
   `r fmt(mrow("SEIR v5", "real interval score"), 0)` vs `r fmt(mrow("ABC-SMC", "real interval score"), 0)`, lower is better), ahead of
   ABC-MCMC (`r fmt(mrow("ABC-MCMC", "real interval score"), 0)`), Nelder-Mead (`r fmt(mrow("NelderMead", "real interval score"), 0)`) and DE
   (`r fmt(mrow("DE", "real interval score"), 0)`), but ABC-SMC needs `r fmt(mrow("ABC-SMC", "seconds per curve"), 0)` s per curve and ran out of
   its simulation budget on `r acc$failed[acc$method == "ABC-SMC"]` of the 100 simulated curves.
4. A bug in the package's Nelder-Mead (its first search step could be almost zero, so it
   stopped at its starting point) was fixed on 2026-10-04 and all affected Nelder-Mead
   results were re-run; earlier reports that showed Nelder-Mead failing on SEIR and
   no-day-0 SIR were caused by it.

# Noise-free simulated data, any window length (SEIR and SIR)

Models trained and tested on noise-free simulated epidemics (every new infection counted),
reading 30 to 365 days from the beginning, middle or end of an epidemic. Coverage: share of
days on which the true count is inside the 95% band of 100 simulations started from the
model's estimated state (`Clean_any_length.Rmd`; reports in `seir_clean/` and `sir_clean/`).

```{r clean, results="asis"}
for (m in c("seir", "sir")) {
  s <- rd(paste0(m, "_clean"), "summary.csv")
  if (is.null(s)) next
  cat(tab(s, col.names = c("window length", "R0 MAE (beginning)", "R0 MAE (all positions)", "true R0 in 95% range (%)",
                           "coverage %: new infections", "coverage %: currently infected"),
          caption = paste(toupper(m), "on noise-free data")), sep = "\n")
}
```

```{r clean-figs, out.width="100%"}
fig("seir_clean", "figures", c("r0-plot-1.png", "coverage-by-day-plot-1.png", "coverage-by-day-plot-2.png"))
fig("sir_clean", "figures", c("r0-plot-1.png", "coverage-by-day-plot-1.png", "coverage-by-day-plot-2.png"))
```

## On real data (30-180-day windows) vs the search methods

The noise-free models on the real datasets, with ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC, Nelder-Mead and DE
estimating the same unknowns (R0 and the state on the window's first day)
(`Clean_real_data.Rmd`; report in `clean_real_data/`). No true R0 here: coverage of the
observed daily counts and the interval score (lower is better).

```{r clean-real, results="asis", eval=file.exists(file.path(R, "clean_real_data", "summary.csv"))}
cat(tab(rd("clean_real_data", "summary.csv"), digits = 2,
        col.names = c("model", "method", "windows", "failed", "mean coverage %", "mean interval score",
                      "lowest score in (windows)", "seconds per window")), sep = "\n")
b <- rd("clean_real_data", "summary_by_length.csv")
for (M in c("SEIR", "SIR")) {
  w <- reshape(b[b$model == M, c("method", "length", "interval_score")], idvar = "method", timevar = "length", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("interval_score.", "", names(w), fixed = TRUE)
  cat(tab(w, digits = 0, caption = paste(M, ": mean interval score by window length (days)")), sep = "\n")
}
```

# SIR models

## Reproducing the original pretrained SIR BiLSTM

Same settings as the pretrained model (incidence divided by 10,000; sigmoid/softplus
outputs; learning rate 2.77e-4; 3 x 160 BiLSTM; dropout 0.5), trained on GPU. With 60,000
training curves (75,000 simulations), R0 matches the pretrained model; the remaining
difference is run-to-run variation (the pretrained model sits inside the spread of seeds).

```{r sir-reproduce}
s75 <- rd("reproduce_pretrained_sir_75k", "seed_variation.csv")
s60 <- rd("reproduce_pretrained_sir", "seed_variation.csv")
s60$model <- sub("New", "48,000 training curves", s60$model)
s75$model <- sub("New", "60,000 training curves", s75$model)
tab(rbind(s75[, c("model", "R0_MAE", "R0_R2", "utah_R0")],
          s60[s60$model != "Pretrained", c("model", "R0_MAE", "R0_R2", "utah_R0")]),
    col.names = c("model", "R0 MAE", "R0 R2", "Utah R0"))
```

```{r sir-reproduce-fig, out.width="85%"}
fig("reproduce_pretrained_sir_75k", "figures", "test-scatter-1.png")
```

## Tuning, day 0, and a wider prior

- **Tuning** (Optuna, 20-epoch trials) found faster settings, but they were unstable over
  100 epochs (R0 MAE 0.055 to 0.117 depending on the seed).
- **Day 0.** The SIR curves started with the number initially infected (a stock) followed
  by new cases (a flow), which made the rebuilt Utah curve drop from 50 to about 10 on
  day 1. Training without day 0 removed the drop, with the same accuracy.

```{r sir-variants}
sir_rows <- list(
  list("Reference (60,000 curves, with day 0)", "reproduce_pretrained_sir_75k", "New"),
  list("Without day 0", "sir_no_day0_75k", "No day 0"),
  list("Without day 0, wider prior (R0 0.5-5)", "sir_no_day0_wide", "No day 0")
)
tab(do.call(rbind, lapply(sir_rows, function(r) {
  tm <- rd(r[[2]], "test_metrics.csv"); u <- rd(r[[2]], "utah_fit_metrics.csv")
  data.frame(model = r[[1]], R0_MAE = r0_row(tm)$MAE[nrow(r0_row(tm))], R0_R2 = r0_row(tm)$R2[nrow(r0_row(tm))],
             utah_coverage_pct = u$coverage_pct[u$model == r[[3]]])
})), col.names = c("model", "R0 MAE", "R0 R2", "Utah coverage %"))
tuned <- rd("sir_bilstm_tuned", "seed_variation.csv")
tab(tuned[, c("model", "R0_MAE", "R0_R2")], col.names = c("model", "R0 MAE", "R0 R2"),
    caption = "Tuned SIR settings, three seeds")
```

With 5,000 people, no constant-parameter SIR curve can stay flat at about 30 cases a day
for 60 days (that would infect 36% of the population), so every method reaches only about
45-50% coverage on the Utah series.

## SIR BiLSTM vs search-based methods

100 simulated test curves; Utah COVID-19 (last 61 days). Nelder-Mead in the
no-day-0 comparison was re-run after the 2026-10-04 bug fix (it used to stop at its start).

```{r sir-methods}
m1 <- rd("sir_method_comparison", "summary.csv")
m2 <- rd("sir_no_day0_method_comparison", "summary.csv")
cols <- c("method", "R0_MAE", "R0_R2", "seconds_per_curve", "utah_coverage_pct", "test_band_coverage_pct")
nm <- c("method", "R0 MAE", "R0 R2", "seconds per curve", "Utah coverage %", "test band coverage %")
tab(m1[, cols], col.names = nm, caption = "With day 0")
tab(m2[, cols], col.names = nm, caption = "Without day 0")
```


# SEIR models on complete counts

Known: `n`, `recov`, `incub`; estimated: ptran, crate, R0 (and, from v2, the share
initially exposed).

```{r seir-models}
seir_rows <- list(
  list("SIR recipe, 75,000 simulations", "seir_bilstm_75k"),
  list("Tuned settings (Optuna)", "seir_bilstm_tuned"),
  list("SEIR v2: 300,000 simulations, share exposed estimated, 5-seed average", "seir_bilstm_v2")
)
tab(do.call(rbind, lapply(seir_rows, function(r) {
  tm <- r0_row(rd(r[[2]], "test_metrics.csv")); u <- rd(r[[2]], "utah_fit_metrics.csv")
  data.frame(model = r[[1]], R0_MAE = tm$MAE, R0_R2 = tm$R2, utah_coverage_pct = u$coverage_pct[u$model == "SEIR"])
})), col.names = c("model", "R0 MAE (test)", "R0 R2", "Utah coverage %"))
```


## Real data with v2 and v3

```{r seir-real}
s <- rd("seir_v2_vs_v3_windows", "summary.csv")
tab(s, digits = 2, caption = "Utah COVID-19 2024-25 61-day windows, and simulated windows from the beginning, middle and end of epidemics")
tab(rd("seir_real_data_test", "summary.csv"), digits = 2,
    caption = "Other real data, 61 days to a week after the peak: coverage % (first three columns) and R0")
```

v2 is better on Utah COVID-19 but poor on the flu data: its smallest starting share
exposed (1%) is far too high for flu hospital admissions (0-17 a day).

# SEIR on reported cases (v4 and v5)

Real data count only some infections and have weekday swings and reporting spikes, which
v2 never saw. v4 and v5 are trained on **reported cases**:

| | v2 | v4 | v5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Training curves | every case, smooth | reported share 5-100%, weekday swings, extra noise (ranges measured on the real data) | same as v4, but **new noise drawn every epoch** |
| Ranges | share exposed 1-40%, incubation 3-21 days, R0 1-5 | share exposed 0.1-40%, incubation 1-21 days, R0 0.8-5 | same as v4 |
| Network input | cases / 10,000 | log(1 + cases), scaled | same |
| Outputs | ptran, crate, R0, share exposed | ptran, R0, share exposed, reported share, noise, weekday swing (crate computed from R0) | same |
| R0 range | none | 95% range from a 100,000-curve calibration bank | same |

v4 learned its fixed training noise by heart after about 25 epochs; v5 draws new reported
cases from the true curves for every batch, so it never sees the same noise twice. A
second v5 has a bigger network (128 hidden units instead of 64). All are averages of 5
seeds and are tested on the same 1,000 simulated curves.

## Simulated epidemics

```{r rep-test}
rt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(rep_models), function(m) {
  x <- rep_test[[m]]
  data.frame(model = m, reported_all = x$model_R0_MAE[1], reported_inside_v2_range = x$model_R0_MAE[2],
             reported_outside_v2_range = x$model_R0_MAE[3], every_case_v2_test = x$model_R0_MAE[4])
}))
x <- rep_test[[1]]
rt <- rbind(data.frame(model = "SEIR v2", reported_all = x$v2_R0_MAE[1], reported_inside_v2_range = x$v2_R0_MAE[2],
                       reported_outside_v2_range = x$v2_R0_MAE[3], every_case_v2_test = x$v2_R0_MAE[4]), rt)
tab(rt, col.names = c("model", "reported cases: all", "inside v2's ranges", "outside v2's ranges",
                      "v2's test curves (every case)"), caption = "R0 MAE")

outs <- lapply(names(rep_models), function(m) {
  o <- rd(rep_models[[m]], "test_all_outputs.csv")
  if (is.null(o)) o <- rd(rep_models[[m]], "test_all_outputs_v4.csv")
  setNames(o$R2, o$output)
})
tab(data.frame(output = names(outs[[1]]), do.call(cbind, lapply(outs, unname)), check.names = FALSE) |>
      setNames(c("output", names(rep_models))),
    caption = "R2 of every output on the reported-case test curves (log scale for the share exposed, reported share and noise)")

rr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(rep_models), function(m) {
  x <- rd(rep_models[[m]], "R0_range_check.csv")[1, ]
  data.frame(model = m, in_95 = x$in_95_range_pct, in_50 = x$in_50_range_pct, width = x$mean_width_95)
}))
tab(rr, digits = 2, col.names = c("model", "true R0 in 95% range (%)", "true R0 in 50% range (%)", "mean 95% width"))
```

## Real data

For each window: v2's band (every case counted), and each reported-case model's band with
its R0 range and reporting noise.

```{r rep-real}
fits <- lapply(names(rep_models), function(m) {
  f <- rd(rep_models[[m]], "real_data_fits.csv")
  f <- f[f$window != "" & grepl("range", f$band), ]
  data.frame(window = paste(f$dataset, f$window, sep = ", "), model = m, R0 = f[[grep("^R0_(model|v4)$", names(f), value = TRUE)]],
             coverage = f$coverage_pct, score = f$interval_score)
})
v2f <- rd(rep_models[[1]], "real_data_fits.csv")
v2f <- v2f[v2f$window != "" & v2f$band == "v2", ]
v2f <- data.frame(window = paste(v2f$dataset, v2f$window, sep = ", "), model = "SEIR v2", R0 = v2f$R0_v2,
                  coverage = v2f$coverage_pct, score = v2f$interval_score)
allf <- rbind(v2f, do.call(rbind, fits))
wide <- function(col) {
  w <- reshape(allf[, c("window", "model", col)], idvar = "window", timevar = "model", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub(paste0(col, "."), "", names(w), fixed = TRUE)
  w
}
tab(wide("coverage"), digits = 1, caption = "Coverage % of the 95% band")
tab(wide("score"), digits = 1, caption = "Interval score (lower is better)")
tab(wide("R0"), digits = 2, caption = "R0 estimates")
us <- lapply(names(rep_models), function(m) {
  u <- rd(rep_models[[m]], "utah_windows_summary.csv")
  data.frame(model = m, band = u$band, coverage = u$mean_fit_coverage_pct, score = u$mean_fit_interval_score)
})
us <- do.call(rbind, us)
us <- rbind(us[us$band == "v2", ][1, ], us[us$band != "v2", ])
us$model[us$band == "v2"] <- "SEIR v2"
tab(us[, c("model", "band", "coverage", "score")], digits = 1,
    caption = "Utah COVID-19 2024-25: mean over 24 windows of 61 days (one every 14 days)")
```

```{r rep-real-figs, out.width="100%"}
fig(rep_models[[best_rep]], "figures", sprintf("real-plots-%d.png", 4:7))
```

# Reported cases: BiLSTM vs ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC, Nelder-Mead and DE

Every method gets the same known values (`n`, `recov`, `incub`) and the same unknowns and
ranges (R0, share exposed, reported share, noise, weekday swing); the search methods use
the package defaults and search the log-scale parameters on the log scale. 100 simulated
test curves of reported cases, and the 7 real windows.

```{r methods-summary}
tab(meth, caption = "Summary (sim = simulated test curves; real = mean over the 7 real windows)")
tab(rd("seir_v4_method_comparison", "accuracy_simulated.csv"),
    caption = "Accuracy on the simulated test curves (errors on the log scale for the share exposed and the reported share)")
tab(rd("seir_v4_method_comparison", "curve_recovery_simulated.csv"), digits = 2,
    caption = "Recovering the simulated curves: 95% bands from each method's result")
tab(rd("seir_v4_method_comparison", "time_per_curve.csv"),
    caption = "Time per curve (BiLSTM: 5 seeds plus the R0 range; search methods: one CPU core)")
tab(rd("seir_v4_method_comparison", "real_data_summary.csv"), digits = 2,
    caption = "Real data: mean over the 7 windows; last column: windows where the method had the lowest interval score")
rbm <- rd("seir_v4_method_comparison", "real_data_by_method.csv")
w <- reshape(rbm[, c("window", "method", "interval_score")], idvar = "window", timevar = "method", direction = "wide")
names(w) <- sub("interval_score.", "", names(w), fixed = TRUE)
tab(w, digits = 1, caption = "Interval score in each real window (lower is better)")
```

```{r methods-figs, out.width="100%"}
fig("seir_v4_method_comparison", "figures",
    c("r0-scatter-1.png", "test-band-boxplot-1.png", sprintf("real-plots-%d.png", 1:7)))
```

# SEIR v6: any window length and reported cases

v6 combines v3 and v5 in one model: it reads **30 to 365 days from the beginning, middle
or end** of an epidemic (like v3) and is trained on **reported cases with new noise every
time** (like v5), with v5's wider ranges. It also estimates the reported share, the noise,
the weekday swing and the shares exposed, infectious and recovered at the window start
(on the log scale), and gives an R0 range. Training windows: length drawn between 30 and
365 days, start drawn inside the epidemic's informative days (before its first week
without reported cases).

```{r v6, results="asis", eval=file.exists(file.path(R, "seir_v6", "summary.csv"))}
tab(rd("seir_v6", "summary.csv"), caption = "Summary")
r6 <- rd("seir_v6", "R0_MAE_by_length_and_position.csv")
for (m in unique(r6$model)) {
  w <- reshape(r6[r6$model == m, c("length", "position", "R0_abs_error")], idvar = "length",
               timevar = "position", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("R0_abs_error.", "", names(w), fixed = TRUE)
  cat(tab(w[order(w$length), intersect(c("length", "beginning", "middle", "end"), names(w))],
          caption = paste(m, ": R0 MAE by window length and position (reported cases)")), sep = "\n")
}
tab(rd("seir_v6", "R0_MAE_compared.csv"), caption = "R0 MAE over all windows each model can read, and on the same 61-day windows from the beginning")
tab(rd("seir_v6", "all_outputs.csv"), caption = "v6: R2 of every output over all test windows")
tab(rd("seir_v6", "R0_range_check.csv"), digits = 2, caption = "v6: true R0 inside the 95% range, by window length")
rr <- rd("seir_v6", "real_data.csv")
tab(rr[, c("window", "days", "R0_v6", "R0_v6_low", "R0_v6_high", "reported_share_v6", "coverage_v6",
           "interval_score_v6", "R0_v5", "coverage_v5", "interval_score_v5")], digits = 2,
    col.names = c("window", "days", "R0 v6", "low", "high", "reported share v6", "coverage v6 %", "score v6",
                  "R0 v5", "coverage v5 %", "score v5"), caption = "Real data")
```

## Six US states

Daily COVID-19 cases from the Johns Hopkins University repository (January 2020 to March
2023), scaled to cases per 10,000 people (the model population is a 10,000-person slice of
the state). Three waves per state: v5 and v6 read the 61 days ending a week after the
peak, and v6 also reads the whole wave.

```{r v6-states, results="asis", eval=file.exists(file.path(R, "seir_v6", "states.csv"))}
tab(rd("seir_v6", "states_summary.csv"), digits = 2,
    col.names = c("fit", "mean coverage %", "mean interval score", "mean width of the R0 range"),
    caption = "Mean over 6 states x 3 waves")
s6 <- rd("seir_v6", "states.csv")
for (col in c("coverage", "interval_score", "R0")) {
  w <- reshape(s6[, c("state", "wave", "fit", col)], idvar = c("state", "wave"), timevar = "fit", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub(paste0(col, "."), "", names(w), fixed = TRUE)
  cat(tab(w, digits = if (col == "R0") 2 else 1,
          caption = c(coverage = "Coverage % of the 95% band", interval_score = "Interval score (lower is better)",
                      R0 = "R0 estimates")[[col]]), sep = "\n")
}
```

```{r v6-figs, out.width="100%", eval=file.exists(file.path(R, "seir_v6", "summary.csv"))}
fig("seir_v6", "figures", c("grid-plot-1.png", sprintf("real-plots-%d.png", 1:17), sprintf("states-plots-%d.png", 1:6)))
```

# SIR v6: any window length and reported cases

The SIR version of SEIR v6, built the same way (same training steps, network settings,
R0 range, real data and states). Known values: `n` and `recov`. The two earlier SIR models
were trained on every case, not on reported cases.

```{r sir-v6, results="asis", eval=file.exists(file.path(R, "sir_v6", "summary.csv"))}
tab(rd("sir_v6", "summary.csv"), caption = "Summary")
r7 <- rd("sir_v6", "R0_MAE_by_length_and_position.csv")
for (m in unique(r7$model)) {
  w <- reshape(r7[r7$model == m, c("length", "position", "R0_abs_error")], idvar = "length",
               timevar = "position", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("R0_abs_error.", "", names(w), fixed = TRUE)
  cat(tab(w[order(w$length), intersect(c("length", "beginning", "middle", "end"), names(w))],
          caption = paste(m, ": R0 MAE by window length and position (reported cases)")), sep = "\n")
}
tab(rd("sir_v6", "R0_MAE_compared.csv"), caption = "R0 MAE over all windows each model can read, and on the same 61-day windows from the beginning")
tab(rd("sir_v6", "all_outputs.csv"), caption = "SIR v6: every output over all test windows, with baselines for ptran and crate")
tab(rd("sir_v6", "R0_range_check.csv"), digits = 2, caption = "SIR v6: true R0 inside the 95% range, by window length")
rs <- rd("sir_v6", "real_data.csv")
tab(rs, digits = 2, col.names = c("window", "days", "R0 SIR v6", "low", "high", "reported share", "coverage %", "score",
                                  "R0 SEIR v6", "coverage % SEIR v6", "score SEIR v6"),
    caption = "Real data: SIR v6 next to SEIR v6")
tab(rd("sir_v6", "states_summary.csv"), digits = 2,
    col.names = c("fit", "coverage % SIR v6", "score SIR v6", "coverage % SEIR v6", "score SEIR v6"),
    caption = "Six states: mean over 18 waves")
ss <- rd("sir_v6", "states.csv")
tab(ss[ss$fit == "v6, whole wave", c("state", "wave", "R0_sir", "coverage_sir", "interval_score_sir", "R0_seir",
                                     "coverage_seir", "interval_score_seir")], digits = 2,
    col.names = c("state", "wave", "R0 SIR v6", "coverage %", "score", "R0 SEIR v6", "coverage %", "score"),
    caption = "Six states, whole waves")
```

```{r sir-v6-figs, out.width="100%", eval=file.exists(file.path(R, "sir_v6", "summary.csv"))}
fig("sir_v6", "figures", c("grid-plot-1.png", sprintf("states-plots-%d.png", 1:6)))
```

# ptran and crate

Only R0 = ptran x crate / recov shapes an epidemic curve: 10 contacts a day with a 2% chance
of passing the infection gives the same curve as 5 contacts with 4%. So ptran and crate
cannot be recovered separately. The baseline knows the true R0 and makes the best guess
for the split (ptran = R0 x recov x the average of 1/crate over its range; crate = the
middle of its range). A model is only better than the baseline if the curve tells it
something about the split.

```{r ptran-crate}
r2 <- function(p, y) 1 - sum((p - y)^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2)
pc_row <- function(model, ep, ec, tp, tc, tR0, recov, lo, hi) data.frame(
  model = model, ptran_MAE = mean(abs(ep - tp)), ptran_R2 = r2(ep, tp),
  baseline_ptran_R2 = r2(tR0 * recov * log(hi / lo) / (hi - lo), tp),
  crate_MAE = mean(abs(ec - tc)), crate_R2 = r2(ec, tc), baseline_crate_MAE = mean(abs((lo + hi) / 2 - tc)))
a <- rd("reproduce_pretrained_sir_75k", "test_predictions.csv")
d <- rd("sir_no_day0_75k", "test_predictions.csv")
v <- rd("seir_bilstm_v2", "test_predictions.csv")
pc <- rbind(
  pc_row("SIR, original pretrained", a$pretrained_ptran, a$pretrained_crate, a$true_ptran, a$true_crate, a$true_R0, a$recov, 1, 5),
  pc_row("SIR, reproduced (reference)", a$new_ptran, a$new_crate, a$true_ptran, a$true_crate, a$true_R0, a$recov, 1, 5),
  pc_row("SIR without day 0", d$estimated_ptran, d$estimated_crate, d$true_ptran, d$true_crate, d$true_R0, d$recov, 1, 5),
  pc_row("SEIR v2", v$estimated_ptran, v$estimated_crate, v$true_ptran, v$true_crate, v$true_R0, v$recov, 5, 15)
)
tab(pc, caption = "Test curves (every case counted). SIR v6 on reported cases: see its table above.")
```

# Conclusions

```{r conclusion-numbers}
u5 <- rd("seir_bilstm_v5", "utah_windows_summary.csv")
u4 <- rd("seir_bilstm_v4", "utah_windows_summary.csv")
```

- **SIR.** The pretrained SIR BiLSTM is reproduced (same settings, 60,000 training curves).
  Dropping day 0 from the SIR curves removes the artificial drop on day 1 at no cost in
  accuracy. For the flat Utah series every method is limited by the model itself (a
  constant-parameter SIR in 5,000 people cannot stay flat for 60 days).
- **SEIR, every case counted.** SEIR v2 (300,000 simulations, tuned settings, starting share
  estimated, 5 seeds) is the most accurate model on simulated curves and beats all search
  methods.
- **SEIR on real data.** Real curves are reported cases. v5 (trained on reported cases, new
  noise each epoch) is the model to use: compared with v4 it lowers the R0 error
  (`r fmt(get(v4, "R0 MAE, new test bank (reported cases)", "model"))` to
  `r fmt(get(v5, "R0 MAE, new test bank (reported cases)", "model"))` on reported-case curves) and fits the 24 Utah COVID-19 windows
  much better (coverage `r fmt(u4$mean_fit_coverage_pct[3], 0)`% to `r fmt(u5$mean_fit_coverage_pct[3], 0)`%, interval score
  `r fmt(u4$mean_fit_interval_score[3], 0)` to `r fmt(u5$mean_fit_interval_score[3], 0)`); v2's are `r fmt(u5$mean_fit_coverage_pct[1], 0)`% and `r fmt(u5$mean_fit_interval_score[1], 0)`.
  A bigger network (128 hidden units) did not help.
- **What can and cannot be recovered.** R0, the share initially exposed and the reported
  share are recovered well (R2 about 0.93, 0.95 and 0.81). ptran and crate separately
  cannot be: only their product (R0 x recov) shapes the curve. The noise level and the
  weekday swing are only partly recoverable (R2 about 0.6 and 0.5).
- **Any window length (v6).** One model now reads 30 to 365 days from any part of an
  epidemic of reported cases. Longer windows give better R0 (R0 MAE about 0.5 at 30 days,
  0.27 at 61 days, 0.06 at 270-365 days); on 61 days from the beginning v5 is still a little
  better (0.23 vs 0.27). It fits single waves well, whole flu seasons and the waves of six
  US states (mean coverage about 95%), but not a whole year with several waves (Utah's last
  180-365 days): one constant R0 cannot make several waves.
- **SIR v6.** The SIR version reads any length too and is more accurate on simulated SIR
  epidemics than SEIR v6 is on SEIR ones (R0 MAE 0.12 vs 0.27 on 61 days from the
  beginning; SIR has no incubation period to estimate). On real data and the six states it
  fits as well as SEIR v6, but gives a lower R0 (about 1.2-1.8 vs 1.2-2.6): without an
  incubation period the same growth needs a smaller R0. The curves cannot tell which
  structure is right, so the R0 value depends on that choice.
- **ptran and crate.** Only their product (R0) can be learned from a curve; crate is not
  recovered by any model or method (R2 at or below 0), and ptran is no better than knowing
  R0 (SIR curves add a little, about 0.60 vs 0.49).
- **Where the search methods still help.** On the rising Utah COVID-19 waves ABC-SMC and
  ABC-MCMC fit the curve better than v5, with a higher R0 but very wide R0 ranges. A
  natural next step is to combine the two: start ABC-SMC inside v5's R0 range, which
  should keep most of the speed and add the curve-matching of ABC.
